arxiv-2007-07630.title: Learning Multiplicative Interactions with Bayesian Neural Networks for Visual-Inertial Odometry
arxiv-2007-07630.creator: Kashmira Shinde, Jongseok Lee, Matthias Humt, Aydin Sezgin, Rudolph Triebel, Kashmira Shinde, Jongseok Lee, Matthias Humt, Aydin Sezgin, Rudolph Triebel
arxiv-2007-07630.description: Abstract This paper presents an end-to-end multi-modal learning approach for monocular Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO), which is specifically designed to exploit sensor complementarity in the light of sensor degradation scenarios. The proposed network makes use of a multi-head self-attention mechanism that learns multiplicative interactions between multiple streams of information.

arxiv-2109-13548.title: Jump rope vortex flow in liquid metal Rayleigh-Bénard convection in a cuboid container of aspect ratio five
arxiv-2109-13548.creator: Megumi Akashi 1, Takatoshi Yanagisawa 2, Ataru Sakuraba 3, Felix Schindler 1, Susanne Horn 4, Tobias Vogt 1, Sven Eckert 1
arxiv-2109-13548.description: Abstract We study the topology and the temporal dynamics of turbulent Rayleigh-Bénard convection in a liquid metal with a Prandtl number of 0.03 located inside a box with a square base area and an aspect ratio of Γ = 5 \Gamma=5 . Experiments and numerical simulations are focused on the Rayleigh number range, 6.

arxiv-2204-11122.title: Can domain adaptation make object recognition work for everyone?
arxiv-2204-11122.creator: Viraj Prabhu, Ramprasaath R. Selvaraju, Judy Hoffman, Nikhil Naik
arxiv-2204-11122.description: Abstract Despite the rapid progress in deep visual recognition, modern computer vision datasets significantly overrepresent the developed world and models trained on such datasets underperform on images from unseen geographies. We investigate the effectiveness of unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) of such models across geographies at closing this performance gap.

arxiv-2303-04621.title: Slip and twinning in Bravais lattices Journal: Journal of Elasticity
arxiv-2303-04621.creator: John M. Ball
arxiv-2303-04621.description: Abstract A unified treatment of slip and twinning in Bravais lattices is given, focussing on the case of cubic symmetry, and using the Ericksen energy well formulation, so that interfaces correspond to rank-one connections between the infinitely many crystallographically equivalent energy wells. Twins are defined to be such rank-one connections involving a nontrivial reflection of the lattice across some plane.

arxiv-2307-07655.title: Toy model illustrating the effect of measurement dependence on a Bell inequality
arxiv-2307-07655.creator: Sophia M. Walls and Ian J. Ford
arxiv-2307-07655.description: Abstract Bell’s inequalities rely on the assumption of measurement independence, namely that the probabilities of adopting configurations of hidden variables describing a system prior to measurement are independent of the choice of physical property that will be measured. Weakening this assumption can change the inequalities to accommodate experimental data.

arxiv-2404-18260.title: Align, Minimize and Diversify: A Source-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation Method for Handwritten Text Recognition
arxiv-2404-18260.creator: María Alfaro-Contreras, Jorge Calvo-Zaragoza
arxiv-2404-18260.description: Abstract This paper serves to introduce the Align, Minimize and Diversify (AMD) method, a Source-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation approach for Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR). This framework decouples the adaptation process from the source data, thus not only sidestepping the resource-intensive retraining process but also making it possible to leverage the wealth of pre-trained knowledge encoded in modern Deep Learning architectures.

arxiv-2411-04641.title: A matter of shape
arxiv-2411-04641.creator: Joaquin Garcia-Suarez
arxiv-2411-04641.description: Abstract Abstract I consider the fluid-mediated approach of a deformable elastic object (“indenter”) to a rigid surface at relatively low velocity. As a fluid is squeezed between the tip and the rigid substrate, lubrication pressures develop, which in turn deform the indenter leading edge. I study the influence of the tip geometry over the lubrication pressure distribution.

arxiv-2501-00953.title: Prior Lessons of Incremental Dialogue and Robot Action Management for the Age of Language Models
arxiv-2501-00953.creator: Casey Kennington \email caseykennington@boisestate.edu, \name Pierre Lison \email plison@nr.no, \name David Schlangen \email david.schlangen@uni-potsdam.de
arxiv-2501-00953.description: Abstract Efforts towards endowing robots with the ability to speak have benefited from recent advancements in natural language processing, in particular large language models. However, current language models are not fully incremental, as their processing is inherently monotonic and thus lack the ability to revise their interpretations or output in light of newer observations.

pmc-10575851.title: Prognostic indices in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: a population-based comparison and validation study of multiple models
pmc-10575851.creator: Jelena Jelicic, Karen Juul-Jensen, Zoran Bukumiric, Michael Roost Clausen, Ahmed Ludvigsen Al-Mashhadi, Robert Schou Pedersen, Christian Bjørn Poulsen, Peter Brown, Tarec Christoffer El-Galaly, Thomas Stauffer Larsen
pmc-10575851.description: Currently, the International Prognostic Index (IPI) is the most used and reported model for prognostication in patients with newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). IPI-like variations have been proposed, but only a few have been validated in different populations (e.g., revised IPI (R-IPI), National Comprehensive Cancer Network IPI (NCCN-IPI)).

pmc-11338284.title: Rediscovering the human thymus through cutting-edge technologies
pmc-11338284.creator: Francesca Pala, Luigi D. Notarangelo, Marita Bosticardo
pmc-11338284.description: This review highlights how novel cutting-edge technologies, including high-resolution imaging, single-cell omics, and organoid cultures, have improved our understanding of human thymus biology, in terms of developmental trajectories, cellular heterogeneity, and spatial organization. Introduction The human thymus has long captivated the interest of researchers due to its crucial role in T cell maturation and immune tolerance.

pmc-11399788.title: Unexpected consequences: Post-traumatic parotid sialocele following facial stab injury: A case report
pmc-11399788.creator: Mehdi Hosseinzadeh, Elaheh Rahimipour, Narges Mirzania, Mahsa Mohammadpour
pmc-11399788.description: Parotid sialocele is characterized by a collection of saliva in the soft tissue surrounding the parotid gland. Etiology may be traumatic, iatrogenic, or laceration to the salivary duct or the gland parenchyma itself. We here report the case of a 40-year-old male patient who presented with a primary complaint of swelling on the right side of his face.

pmc-11446925.title: Fabric-based lamina emergent MXene-based electrode for electrophysiological monitoring
pmc-11446925.creator: Sanghyun Lee, Dong Hae Ho, Janghwan Jekal, Soo Young Cho, Young Jin Choi, Saehyuck Oh, Yoon Young Choi, Taeyoon Lee, Kyung-In Jang, Jeong Ho Cho
pmc-11446925.description: Commercial wearable biosignal sensing technologies encounter challenges associated with irritation or discomfort caused by unwanted objects in direct contact with the skin, which can discourage the widespread adoption of wearable devices. To address this issue, we propose a fabric-based lamina emergent MXene-based electrode, a lightweight and flexible shape-morphing wearable bioelectrode.

pmc-11452348.title: Whole cell affinity for 4‐amino‐5‐hydroxymethyl‐2‐methylpyrimidine (HMP) in the marine bacterium Candidatus Pelagibacter st. HTCC7211 explains marine dissolved HMP concentrations
pmc-11452348.creator: Elizabeth Brennan, Stephen Noell, Edward W Davis, Stephen J Giovannoni, Christopher P Suffridge
pmc-11452348.description: Vitamin B1 is a universally required coenzyme in carbon metabolism. However, most marine microorganisms lack the complete biosynthetic pathway for this compound and must acquire thiamin, or precursor molecules, from the dissolved pool. The most common version of Vitamin B1 auxotrophy is for thiamin's pyrimidine precursor moiety, 4‐amino‐5‐hydroxymethyl‐2‐methylpyrimidine (HMP).

pmc-12454396.title: The impact of telework on absenteeism, presenteeism, and return to work among workers with health conditions: a scoping review
pmc-12454396.creator: Julien Ducas, Catherine Daneau, Salma Bouqartacha, Alexandra Lecours, Jacques Abboud, Andrée-Anne Marchand, Martin Descarreaux
pmc-12454396.description: IntroductionTelework has become increasingly prominent as a flexible work arrangement, particularly since the COVID-19 pandemic. For workers managing health conditions, it may support continued employment by influencing key work-related phenomena such as absenteeism, presenteeism and return to work (RTW) process.

pmc-12503944.title: Transcriptomic and metabolomic insights into light-mediated unicellular-to-multicellular transition in Dictyostelium discoideum
pmc-12503944.creator: Yuehui Tian, Huiru Liu, Shanshan Xu, Zihe Wang, Zhili He, Ruiqi Liu, Longfei Shu
pmc-12503944.description: both unicellular and multicellular cells would allow us to understand the mechanisms that regulate this critical transition. Dictyostelium discoideum contains different cell types during the life cycle, including solitary vegetative cells germinated from spores, multicellular slugs and fruiting bodies with new spores [1].

pmc-12506129.title: Analysing the effect of multidisciplinary teams to address preventive healthcare gaps in a rural teaching clinic: a quality improvement project
pmc-12506129.creator: Veronica Hill, Brittany Woody, Fahad Irfan Abid, Meaghan Barros, Priya Pohani
pmc-12506129.description: Preventive care decreases the risk of illness, disease and death, yet patient adherence to preventive care is low, calculated to be around 5%, and rural residents are suspected to have even lower rates compared with urban patients. Despite continually updated guidelines and recommendations for screenings and preventive care, delivery of care to rural patients is difficult, and a deficit exists.

pmc-12735019.title: Effects of Invasive Solidago canadensis and Biochar on the Remediation of Soil Cd Contamination and Greenhouse Gas Emissions
pmc-12735019.creator: Xiaokang Ni, Yadi Yu, Xi Liu, Wanqing Nie, Yuli Hu, Jian Bai, Ziyi Yan, Wei Li, Lifei Xiong, Xixian Xie, Yuanyuan Zhu, Zihan Zeng, Qingye Yu, Shuli Wang, Qin Ying, Nansheng Wu, Ling Zhang, Balazs Barna
pmc-12735019.description: Cadmium (Cd) contamination in agricultural soils threatens food security and exacerbates climate change through its impact on greenhouse gas (GHG) (CO2, N2O and CH4) emissions, in which N2O and CO2 are the dominant fluxes of the terrestrial carbon-nitrogen cycle whose magnitude is directly amplified by Cd stress. Key remediation approaches for this dual challenge are phytoremediation and biochar amendment.

pmc-12869914.title: Association between serum copper concentration and type 2 diabetes mellitus in elderly people in Northeast China: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12869914.creator: Xiaonan Li, Li Yang, Dongmei Mu, Yuehui Wang
pmc-12869914.description: BackgroundNumerous studies have demonstrated a significant association between serum copper (Cu) levels and abnormal glucose metabolism. However, there is a notable lack of research specifically examining the relationship between serum Cu concentration and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in the elderly population. Consequently, this study aims to investigate the potential association between serum Cu concentration and T2DM in elderly adults.

pmc-13219460.title: Spontaneous eye blink rate indicates increased attention during grooming in female Barbary macaques
pmc-13219460.creator: J Ostner, R Honnavara, C Bruchmann, O Schülke
pmc-13219460.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Spontaneous eye blinking is a ubiquitous behavior in animals including humans necessary for lubricating the ocular surface and preventing dryness. Beyond this functional role, eye blinking also provides a window into an animal’s cognitive state and attention allocation.

pmc-13283711.title: Age and Sex-Based Differences in Confidence, Emotion and Risk Appraisal after ACL Reconstruction in Pediatric and Adolescent Athletes
pmc-13283711.creator: Matthew Milewski, Emma Gossman, Subrina Farah, Dai Sugimoto, Mininder Kocher, Dennis Kramer, Yi-Meng Yen, Melissa Christino
pmc-13283711.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:Psychological readiness after ACL reconstruction (ACLR) in young athletes has been shown to affect return to sports, knee function, and patient-reported outcomes, and has been associated with age and sex differences in young patients.

pmc-13534770.title: Cardiac lesions in sheep and goats with spontaneous Clostridium perfringens type D enterotoxemia
pmc-13534770.creator: Emma H. Torii, Omar A. Gonzales-Viera, Jennine Ochoa, Todd Cornish, Nicolas Streitenberger, Roberto W. I. Olivares, Hannah Neer, Francisco A. Uzal, Asli Mete
pmc-13534770.description: A 12-year retrospective search identified 106 sheep and goats diagnosed with Clostridium perfringens type D enterotoxemia, and in which the heart was histologically examined. Twenty cases (20/106, 19%), including 10 sheep and 10 goats, had cardiac lesions that were presumed to be associated with enterotoxemia.

pmc-13572552.title: Uncovering the genomic landscape of Mycobacterium bovis in Wales
pmc-13572552.creator: Amy J E Healey, Cate L Williams, Nicholas J Dimonaco, Terry Galloway, Richard J Ellis, Eleftheria Palkopoulou, James Strong, Amanda J Gibson, R Glyn Hewinson, Jessica C A Friedersdorff
pmc-13572552.description: Bovine tuberculosis (bTB), caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium bovis, is one of the most pressing animal health issues in Wales today. It negatively impacts cattle health, affects profitability and trade, and can decimate years of genetic improvement towards desirable production traits. It also imposes substantial financial, social, and psychological burdens on farming communities.

pmc-13597283.title: Protocol for high-sensitivity detection of microRNAs in adult Drosophila tissues using hybridization chain reaction
pmc-13597283.creator: Sneh Harsh, Amelie A Raz, Erika A Bach
pmc-13597283.description: SummaryMicroRNAs (miRNAs) are post-transcriptional regulators of gene expression and cell-fate determination. Here, we present a protocol for detecting miRNAs in Drosophila gonadal tissues using an optimized hybridization chain reaction (HCR)-based approach. We describe steps for using modular probes and antibody-free signal amplification to visualize miRNAs while preserving tissue morphology and spatial resolution.

uslaw-usc-t20-s4501.title: 20 U.S.C. § 4501 — Purpose
uslaw-usc-t20-s4501.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t20-s4501.description: United States Code, Title 20 (Education); Chapter 57 (James Madison Memorial Fellowship Program). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. It is the purpose of this chapter to establish the James Madison Fellowship Program which is designed to encourage graduate study of the American Constitution, its roots, its formation, its principles, and its development.
